title: Proper fibre idempotents come from the pushforward stalk
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $s\in S$, and let $e\in H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$ be an idempotent on the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Then $e$ lies in the image of $(f_*\mathcal O_X)_s\to H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 21.16.1 (Tag 0G7X), statement and proof lines 8117--8179

proof.text: (Noetherian case, setup.) In Steps 1-4 assume moreover that $S$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Put $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_s$, $M=(f_*\mathcal O_X)_s$ (an $A$-module) and, for $n\ge1$, $A_n=A/\mathfrak m^n$, $X_n=\operatorname{Spec}A_n\times_SX$, so that $X_1=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\times_SX$ is the fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] (up to the symmetry of the fibre product). By the definition of locally Noetherian, $s$ lies in an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq S$ with $B$ Noetherian; $A=B_{\mathfrak p}$ for the prime $\mathfrak p$ of $s$, so $A$ is a Noetherian local ring [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated.

source.place: proof of Lemma 0G7X, second paragraph ('Assume S is Noetherian'), lines 8128-8132

proof.text: (Lifting $e$ to the infinitesimal neighbourhoods.) For $n\ge1$, $X_1=X_n\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A_n}\operatorname{Spec}(A_n/\mathfrak mA_n)$ (associativity of fibre products, $A_n/\mathfrak mA_n=\kappa(s)$), and the ideal $J=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^n$ of $A_n$ satisfies $J^n=0$. Hence the restriction $\Gamma(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})\to\Gamma(X_1,\mathcal O_{X_1})$ along the closed immersion $X_1\to X_n$ is a bijection on idempotents [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-nilpotent-thickening-idempotents] (this is the statement that $X_n$ and $X_s$ have the same underlying space, so the decomposition $X_s=T_1\amalg T_2$ given by $e$ lifts to $X_n$). Let $e_n\in\Gamma(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$ be the unique idempotent restricting to $e$. For $n\le n'$ the restriction of $e_{n'}$ to $X_n$ is an idempotent whose restriction to $X_1$ is $e$ (the composite $X_1\to X_n\to X_{n'}$ is the closed immersion $X_1\to X_{n'}$), so it equals $e_n$ by uniqueness. Thus $(e_n)_n\in\varprojlim_n H^0(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$, with first component $e_1=e$.

source.place: proof of Lemma 0G7X, lines 8133-8146 ('Since the underlying topological space of X_n is equal to that of X_s ... e_{n+1} restricts to e_n on X_n')

proof.text: (Formal functions.) By the theorem on formal functions at $s$ [lem-weil-pbc-formal-functions-stalk] with $p=0$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ ($f$ proper, $S$ locally Noetherian, $\mathcal O_X$ coherent), the maps $\theta_n:M\to H^0(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$ (pull back a germ of a section of $\mathcal O_X$ over $f^{-1}(V)$ to $X_n$) induce an $A$-linear isomorphism $\theta:M^\wedge\to\varprojlim_nH^0(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$, $M^\wedge=\varprojlim_nM/\mathfrak m^nM$, with $\theta\circ\iota=(\theta_n)_n$ for the canonical map $\iota:M\to M^\wedge$. Note that $\theta_1:M\to H^0(X_1,\mathcal O_{X_1})=H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$ is the map of the statement. Put $e_\infty=\theta^{-1}((e_n)_n)\in M^\wedge$; its image under the first component of $\theta$ is $e$.

source.place: proof of Lemma 0G7X, lines 8132-8149, citing Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02OD (coherent-lemma-formal-functions-stalk)

proof.text: (Descending from the completion.) Since $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated, the projection $p_1:M^\wedge\to M/\mathfrak mM$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak mM^\wedge$, and $p_1\circ\iota$ is the quotient map $M\to M/\mathfrak mM$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] (part (2), $n=1$; this is Algebra 05GG, $M^\wedge/\mathfrak mM^\wedge=M/\mathfrak mM$). Choose $x\in M$ with $p_1(\iota(x))=p_1(e_\infty)$; then $\iota(x)-e_\infty\in\mathfrak mM^\wedge$, so, $\theta$ being $A$-linear, $\theta(\iota(x))-(e_n)_n\in\mathfrak m\cdot\varprojlim_nH^0(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$. Its first component lies in $\mathfrak m\,H^0(X_1,\mathcal O_{X_1})=0$, since $A$ acts on $H^0(X_1,\mathcal O_{X_1})$ through $A\to\kappa(s)$ ($X_1$ is a scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$). Hence $\theta_1(x)=e_1=e$, i.e. $e$ is in the image of $(f_*\mathcal O_X)_s\to H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$. This proves the lemma when $S$ is locally Noetherian.

source.place: proof of Lemma 0G7X, lines 8150-8157, citing Algebra, Lemma 05GG (algebra-lemma-hathat-finitely-generated)

proof.text: (General case: reduction to $S$ affine.) Let $V\subseteq S$ be an affine open neighbourhood of $s$ and $f_V:f^{-1}(V)\to V$ the restriction, the base change of $f$ along the open immersion $V\to S$, hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. The stalk $(f_*\mathcal O_X)_s$ is the colimit of $\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}(W))$ over open $W\ni s$, which may be taken inside $V$, so it equals $(f_{V,*}\mathcal O_{f^{-1}(V)})_s$; and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ factors through $V$, so $X_s=f^{-1}(V)\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], compatibly with the maps to $H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$. Hence we may replace $f$ by $f_V$ and assume $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ affine.

source.place: proof of Lemma 0G7X, third paragraph, line 8163 ('We may replace S by an affine open neighbourhood of s')

proof.text: (Noetherian approximation.) As $S$ is affine, by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-limit-noetherian] (Limits 0A0P, affine clause) there are a directed set $\Lambda$ and an inverse system of proper morphisms $f_\lambda:X_\lambda\to S_\lambda=\operatorname{Spec}A_\lambda$ with affine transition morphisms, $A_\lambda$ a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra, such that $X=\varprojlim X_\lambda$, $S=\varprojlim S_\lambda$ and $f=\varprojlim f_\lambda$. Each $A_\lambda$ is a Noetherian ring [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] (applied to $\mathbf Z\to A_\lambda$, $\mathbf Z$ being a principal ideal domain, hence Noetherian), so each $S_\lambda$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] (covered by the single affine open $S_\lambda$).

source.place: proof of Lemma 0G7X, lines 8165-8168, citing Limits, Lemma 0A0P (limits-lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian)

proof.text: (The fibre as a limit.) Let $s_\lambda\in S_\lambda$ be the image of $s$. Then $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)=\varprojlim_\lambda\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_\lambda)$ over the $S_\lambda$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-residue-field] (Limits 0CUG, $s=\lim s_\lambda$), and therefore the fibres $X_{\lambda,s_\lambda}=X_\lambda\times_{S_\lambda}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_\lambda)$ form an inverse system with affine transition morphisms whose limit is $X_s$, with projections the induced morphisms $q_\lambda:X_s\to X_{\lambda,s_\lambda}$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-fibre-products] (limits commute with limits, Categories 002M). Each $X_{\lambda,s_\lambda}$ is proper over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_\lambda)$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence quasi-compact and separated, the base being affine [pqf-lem-proper-basic], hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated (a closed immersion is quasi-compact, so a separated morphism is quasi-separated).

source.place: proof of Lemma 0G7X, lines 8168-8172, citing Limits, Lemma 0CUG (limits-lemma-inverse-limit-irreducibles) and Categories, Lemma 002M (categories-lemma-colimits-commute)

proof.text: (Descending the idempotent.) By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-global-sections-colimit] (Limits 01Z0 for the structure sheaf), applied to the system $(X_{\lambda,s_\lambda})_\lambda$, $\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})=\varinjlim_\lambda\Gamma(X_{\lambda,s_\lambda},\mathcal O)$ via the $q_\lambda^\sharp$. So $e=q_\lambda^\sharp(a)$ for some $\lambda$ and $a\in\Gamma(X_{\lambda,s_\lambda},\mathcal O)$. Then $q_\lambda^\sharp(a^2-a)=e^2-e=0$, so $a^2-a$ restricts to $0$ on $X_{\mu,s_\mu}$ for some $\mu\ge\lambda$; the restriction $e_\mu$ of $a$ to $X_{\mu,s_\mu}$ is an idempotent with $q_\mu^\sharp(e_\mu)=e$ (the $q$'s are compatible with the transition morphisms).

source.place: proof of Lemma 0G7X, lines 8172-8174, citing Limits, Lemma 01Z0 (limits-lemma-descend-section)

proof.text: (Applying the Noetherian case and pulling back.) By Steps 1-4 applied to the proper morphism $f_\mu:X_\mu\to S_\mu$ over the locally Noetherian $S_\mu$, there is $\tilde e_\mu\in(f_{\mu,*}\mathcal O_{X_\mu})_{s_\mu}$ mapping to $e_\mu$; represent it by $t\in\mathcal O_{X_\mu}(f_\mu^{-1}(W_\mu))$ for an open $W_\mu\ni s_\mu$. Let $p_\mu:X\to X_\mu$, $\pi_\mu:S\to S_\mu$ be the projections and $W=\pi_\mu^{-1}(W_\mu)\ni s$; then $p_\mu^{-1}(f_\mu^{-1}(W_\mu))=f^{-1}(W)$ and $\tilde e=$ the germ at $s$ of $p_\mu^\sharp(t)\in\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}(W))$ lies in $(f_*\mathcal O_X)_s$. The composite $X_s\to f^{-1}(W)\to f_\mu^{-1}(W_\mu)$ equals $X_s\xrightarrow{q_\mu}X_{\mu,s_\mu}\to f_\mu^{-1}(W_\mu)$ (both are the morphism induced by $p_\mu$ on fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre]), so the image of $\tilde e$ in $H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$ is $q_\mu^\sharp(e_\mu)=e$.
